title: Causal Slipproof Instrumentation Bridge for Intermittent Edge Clients
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: mobile and edge clients (intermittent networks, long-polling, websocket reconnects) often lose causal linkages between requests and background retries. Existing SDK hooks can drop span ancestry during reconnects or when the request is retried from a different transport. Goal: implement a lightweight instrumentation bridge that preserves causal relationships across transport-layer slips (reconnects, queued retries, background syncs) with minimal runtime overhead and backward-compatible SDK changes.
implementation_plan: Design an idempotent per-request provenance token (32-byte stable fingerprint + monotonic slip counter) emitted by SDK at request start
Add a compact bridge header 'x-rw-provenance' and a short wire-encoded envelope to carry provenance token and minimal sampling hints
SDK: augment fetch/websocket adapters to attach/restore provenance token on reconnects and queued retry executions
Server runtime: implement a fast provenance stitcher that rehydrates parent-span hints into request context before instrumentation hooks run
Fallback: when provenance token absent, use existing trace header flow (no regressions). Provide an opt-in mode to always enable stitcher for selected routes.
Benchmark and tune: microbench fetch adapter overhead (<150ns avg), wire header <48 bytes, server stitcher CPU <0.2% on p95 workloads
acceptance_criteria: Preserves causal linkage for >=95% of simulated reconnect+retry scenarios in integration tests
End-to-end trace in distributed tracer shows correct parent-child ordering across reconnect boundaries for sample workloads
Overhead: SDK adapter adds <0.2ms p95 on cold path and <150ns on hot path; server stitcher latency budget tested under load
No dropped spans or trace loops introduced; all existing telemetry tests pass
Design doc reviewed and approved by Observability and SDK leads; security review completed
risks: Edge clients may send malformed provenance tokens leading to parsing overhead; mitigate by strict length checks and fast-path rejects
Potential privacy/leakage concerns if provenance tokens correlate to user ids; will avoid PII and rotate token entropy periodically
Rollout complexity: enabling stitcher globally could change trace sampling characteristics; plan staged rollout by route and customer tier
Compatibility: older SDKs that don't emit provenance must still interoperate without regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests for encoder/decoder and header parsing (fuzz targets for malformed tokens)
Integration harness: simulated mobile reconnection patterns (exponential backoff, queued retries, background sync) validating trace continuity
Load test: server stitcher under synthetic p95/p99 traffic; verify CPU and latency impact
Canary: roll out to internal staging and a small subset of low-risk customers with tracing flags enabled
Observability: new dashboards for provenance-stitch-rate, stitch-latency, and stitch-failure-rate
